title: Projects
text:
Selected work
    Projects
    Hands-on analytics work from my MS in Applied Business Analytics at Boston University, where most projects are team-based, plus analytics I lead as a volunteer leader in my community.
  



  
    
      
    
    
      01  /  BIG DATA & CLOUD ANALYTICS
      Job Market Analytics with Spark SQL on AWS
      AD 688 · Fall 2026
      Large datasets don't fit in a spreadsheet, and procurement data rarely does either. Working in a cloud environment on AWS, I used Spark SQL to turn a large dataset of real job postings from BU's MET Career Match data into answers about salaries, employers, and hiring trends.
      
        Loaded the partitioned Parquet dataset into Spark on an AWS EC2 instance
        Designed a relational model of four linked tables (job postings, companies, industries, locations) with primary and foreign keys
        Wrote Spark SQL joins and aggregations to compare median tech salaries by occupation, rank top remote employers in California, track monthly posting trends, and compare pay across 12 major U.S. metros
        Visualized results with Plotly and Seaborn and published a reproducible Quarto report through GitHub
      
      AWS EC2PySparkSpark SQLData modelingPlotlySeabornQuarto
    
  

  
    
      
    
    
      02  /  TEAM PROJECT In progress
      Fashion & Apparel Career Evaluation
      AD 688 · Group 7 · Team of 4
      What does the market for analytics talent look like inside fashion retail? Our team is building a published research site that evaluates business and data analyst roles at apparel and fashion employers (NAICS 458), then compares what employers ask for with our own skills.
      
        Led research and built the filtered industry dataset the team uses for analysis
        Cleaned and standardized core variables: salary, experience, location, and work arrangement
        Early finding: Power BI and SQL are the most requested skills, each appearing in 7 of 19 postings
      
      PythonpandasPlotlyQuartoGitHub
      View project site
    
  

  
    
      
    
    
      03  /  LEADERSHIP
      Community Impact Analytics
      New York Junior League · Community Senior Council Head
      I bring the same analytical discipline I use in procurement to the League's Community area, turning scattered data and feedback into clear decisions.
      
        Meal spend: analyzed meal purchases and recommended where to order from and when catering makes sense
        Volunteer impact: analyzed volunteer hours and activity to give leaders a clearer view of impact
        Partner feedback: analyzed community partners' end-of-year feedback and comments to surface themes
        Partnership health check: designed a new annual process for committees to evaluate the health of each community partnership, and for the League to assess committee health and synergies
      
      Spend analysisText analysisProcess designStakeholder alignment

title: Where procurement strategy meets analytics.
text:
Procurement  ·  Strategy  ·  Analytics
      Where procurement strategy meets analytics.
      I'm Alyssa, a global procurement leader who has built and scaled sourcing organizations across retail, consumer, and digital commerce brands. Today I lead Global Indirect Procurement at Ralph Lauren, and I'm earning an MS in Applied Business Analytics at Boston University to bring sharper data to the decisions procurement makes every day.
      
        View my work
        Read my CV
      
    
    
      
    
  



  
    
      $2BAnnual spend led
      $250M+Cost savings delivered
      6Global consumer brands
    
  



  
    
      Why analytics, why now
      Procurement has always run on data. It just hasn't always used it well.
    
    
      Procurement sits on some of the richest data in any company: every supplier, every contract, every dollar that leaves the building. Yet in my experience, analytics is one of the least invested-in capabilities in the function. Too many sourcing decisions still start in a spreadsheet someone rebuilt from scratch.
      That gap matters more than ever. Supply-chain volatility, cost pressure, and AI are changing how quickly organizations need to see risk and act on opportunity. I went back to school to build the technical foundation (SQL, Spark, cloud platforms, and data visualization) so I can lead that shift rather than wait for it.
    
  



  
    What I bring
    Three lenses, one leader
    
      
        
        Strategic Sourcing
        Category strategy, supplier negotiation, and vendor performance across marketing, technology, logistics, facilities, and corporate services.
      
      
        
        Enterprise Transformation
        Standing up centralized procurement functions, procure-to-pay and ERP rollouts, M&A integration, and the change management that makes them stick.
      
      
        
        Analytics & Insight
        Spend visibility, KPI frameworks, and dashboards, now backed by hands-on work in Python, SQL, Spark, and cloud analytics.
      
    
  



  
    Where I'm headed
    I want to lead procurement organizations where analytics is a core capability, not an afterthought: predictive spend insight, early supplier-risk signals, and decision tools that let teams move faster with confidence.
  



  
    Brands I've built with
    
      TargetStarbucksTapestryRevlonFanaticsRalph Lauren

In my role, I'm working to better capture and report our volunteer impact, bringing the same process and data discipline I use at work to a mission I care about.
